subject: Pilot success rubric, acceptance tests & go-to-close checklist
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot success rubric & next steps (MAP draft)

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great questions from your ML team. As discussed, attaching a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a proposed pilot success rubric so we can align on what 'acceptance' looks like and what will trigger move to procurement.

High level asks / proposed checkpoints:
- Week 0: Kickoff + network/access setup (VPC peering + test dataset uploaded)
- Week 1–2: Inference baseline run (latency, throughput, baseline prompts)
- Week 3: Quality acceptance tests (precision/recall baseline & safety spot checks)
- Week 4: Scale run + cost projection and final decision meeting

Acceptance criteria (draft):
1) Latency: median tail p95 <= 120ms on 2k token sequences under defined load
2) Quality: instruction-following A/B pass rate >= 85% on the agreed prompt set
3) Reliability: 99.9% successful inference rate during test window
4) Security: SOC 2 evidence provided and access control validated

Attachments included: mutual-action-plan-v1.docx and pilot-success-rubric.xlsx (see details per checkpoint).

Next steps: please confirm stakeholders and any extra success metrics you want to include. If OK I’ll schedule a 30-minute checkpoint for Friday to review the rubric.

Best,

Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

- Our procurement team requires a draft MSA and an estimated monthly spend for the scale run by Week 4.
- For quality, can we add a false-positive threshold for our domain-specific entity extraction (<= 10%)?

Stakeholders: myself, Andre Diaz (procurement), and Dr. Priya Shah (ML lead). Please add Andre to the thread.
